UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, arts. 3-4 (UBO definition; 25% ownership threshold and control test), 9 (identification duties), 14 (PEP rules), 25 (record-keeping), 32 (suspicious transaction reporting); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, arts. 3-7; Real Decreto 95/2018, de 30 de marzo, creating the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales; Ley 14/2023, de 18 de mayo, reforming the UBO register access and filing regime applicable to all new SL incorporations; Ley 1/2010 Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) arts. 18 and 22; Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on crypto-asset fund transfer traceability (USDC payment rails); Directive (EU) 2015/849 and (EU) 2018/843 as transposed.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

Accepted for the ISIC 6201 data-pipeline API activity. The SL must denominate a physical Spanish address in the incorporation deed and RMC entry; a virtual-office operator performing mail reception, legal notice service and compliance-address functions is compliant, provided the address is a real place in Spain and the operator is not a mere PO box; no local employees, premises or fixed establishment is statutorily required for a remote API/data business, but the registered office must remain effectively accessible for legal process and AEAT correspondence under art. 18 of Ley de Sociedades de Capital.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central (Central Mercantile Registry), Madrid, for the negative name certificate; Registro Mercantil de Madrid (Provincial Mercantile Registry) for inscription of the public deed; notarial authority for the execution and issuance of the deed.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010, of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), Articles 4.1, 19-22, 23, 33, 62(1), 210, 363 and 367.

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) recorded in the Registro Mercantil, together with Form 036 submitted to the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria for the provisional NIF.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 16 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

For an SL, the minimum share capital is EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,260), fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation. The capital is deposited into a temporary corporate bank account with a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by the bank's certificate of deposit attached to the public deed. There is no statutory escrow account; the funds are released on execution of the deed and are available for corporate activity immediately after registration.

Funding & unlock path: Office premises must satisfy the general fire-safety and occupational-risk requirements of Royal Decree 486/1997 (workplaces). The municipal civil protection department conducts structural-load and fire-prevention inspections only where the rented office is located in an ordinary commercial building; no special industrial or civil-defense permit is required for an API gateway business.

Paid-in capital rule: For an SL, the minimum share capital is EUR 3,000 (approx. USD 3,260), fully subscribed and paid in cash at incorporation. The capital is deposited into a temporary corporate bank account with a Spanish credit institution and evidenced by the bank's certificate of deposit attached to the public deed. There is no statutory escrow account; the funds are released on execution of the deed and are available for corporate activity immediately after registration.

Category: None (statutory license not required for ISIC 6201 digital services); a municipal 'licencia de actividad' for the physical office may be required but is generally exempt for professional offices under R.D. 1008/2010

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and its official portal at www.agenciatributaria.es

E-government filing portal

Foreign entities must obtain a Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by submitting an application to the AEAT, either online via the Cl@ve or certificate methods or in person at an authorized office, requiring identification documents such as passport and proof of address; the process typically takes 10-15 business days for approval.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — Foreign entities must obtain a Spanish NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) by submitting an application to the AEAT, either online via the Cl@ve or certificate methods or in person at an authorized office, requiring identification documents such as passport and proof of address; the process typically takes 10-15 business days for approval.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation

Available election forms

Spain does not offer check-the-box elections; tax classification is determined by residency rules under the Spanish Tax Law and EU directives. Hybrid mismatch elections are available under the ATAD framework for certain cross-border structures.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

30,000 euros annual turnover

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Exports of goods to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT rate upon submission of customs export declaration and proof of actual export; offshore services to non-EU customers are zero-rated if the service is effectively used outside the EU and no establishment is present in Spain.

  • Customs Export Declaration (ED), Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, Proof of Repatriation of Payment (Inward Remittance Certificate)

Mandatory electronic invoicing under Facturae standard for B2B transactions; real-time VAT reporting via the SII (Immediate Supply Information) system for qualifying taxpayers; digital stamping and clearance integrated with AEAT systems.

Fraudulent claims of export zero-rating may result in penalties of up to 100% of the evaded tax, retrospective clawback of zero-rating benefits, and potential criminal prosecution under Spanish tax evasion laws.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Full and unrestricted convertibility of the euro in both current and capital account transactions under Articles 63-66 TFEU and Spain's Ley 19/2003 de Régimen Jurídico de los Movimientos de Capitales y de las Transacciones Económicas con el Exterior. No exchange control authorization is required for inbound equity contributions, dividend repatriation, payments for services, or liquidation proceeds. Transactions exceeding EUR 1,000,000 require ex-post statistical declaration to the Banco de España, but such filing is informational, not a prior approval. Profit remittance is unrestricted and subject only to standard withholding tax compliance and documentary bank KYC on beneficial ownership. There is no blocked capital account regime and no prioritization of current vs capital account approval.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in Spain or abroad, freely converted into euros, or used for treasury management. The only obligation is statistical reporting of cross-border payments and positions when thresholds apply. EU anti-money-laundering rules require full traceability of receipts, and tax law requires invoice transactions to be documented, but there is no percentage surrender quota or statutory repatriation timeline for export collections.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting under the European System of Central Banks, with the Dirección General de Operaciones y Mercados overseeing reserves and payment systems; foreign exchange surveillance and statistical duties are shared with the Secretaría General del Tesoro y Financiación Internacional and the Comisión de Prevención de Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias. The Spanish Ministry of Economy is competent for capital movement restrictions under EU law.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Medium-to-High only as an ancillary rail; not a substitute for a licensed credit institution. Authorized EU/EEA Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) operating in Spain under the PSD2 and Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 may be used for low-balance operational accounts and cross-border collections, provided they hold a passportable license (e.g., to EBA register) and appoint a Spanish AML representative where required. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot offer capital escrow-taking deposit business, cannot extend credit, and client funds must be safeguarded in segregated pools; use of an unlicenced offshore EMI is prohibited and constitutes an AML/institutional red flag. The selected entity must support IBAN, SEPA, SWIFT MT103, and ideally Crypto-to-fiat on/off ramps with compliant CFATF/EBA travel-rule attestation.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

Non-resident director or shareholder resident outside the EU, especially in a jurisdiction featuring high-risk or non-cooperative status.

Root cause: Non-resident director or shareholder resident outside the EU, especially in a jurisdiction featuring high-risk or non-cooperative status.

Defense evidence: Notarized and apostilled passport copies, certificate of good standing, profiles on shareholders, tax residence certificates (Modelo 030/EXR), three months of business bank statements, source of wealth declaration, and a corporate organizational chart supported by a WE-02 Spanish corporate registry extract.
The commercial model is cross-border scraping and API data sales, which can trigger refusal for 'unclear economic purpose' or perceived exposure to data-regulation liability.

Root cause: The commercial model is cross-border scraping and API data sales, which can trigger refusal for 'unclear economic purpose' or perceived exposure to data-regulation liability.

Defense evidence: Comprehensive commercial contract with a named counterparty, customer due-diligence framework, GDPR and Data Commercialization compliance material, SWIFT and wire-flow summaries, a formal Business Plan with realistic turnover projections, and proof that permitted target websites are public APIs with lawful access terms.
Use of cryptocurrency terms in treasury (USDC receipts / crypto-to-fiat settlement), which banks commonly reject outright.

Root cause: Use of cryptocurrency terms in treasury (USDC receipts / crypto-to-fiat settlement), which banks commonly reject outright.

Defense evidence: Blockchain transaction addresses, Chainalysis/ Elliptic due-diligence reports on source-of-funds tokens, a signed AML/CFT policy covering travel-rule compliance, licensing evidence for crypto-fiat processors, and a management letter undertaking that all crypto inflows are converted to fiat only through regulated Spanish or EU exchanges.
High throughput of small-payment commercial API invoices through a single collecting account, resembling layering or invoice-laundering.

Root cause: High throughput of small-payment commercial API invoices through a single collecting account, resembling layering or invoice-laundering.

Defense evidence: Audited monthly invoices and ledgers, historic bank statements of the Spanish SL, signed terms-of-service with API users, and a designated compliance officer questionnaire plus independent AML audit report. Evidence must reconcile every invoice to a settled card/IBAN/crypto transaction without gaps.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Equity subscription proceeds should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's foreign bank to the SL's EUR operational account. For EU-origin wires, use SEPA CT messages with ISO 20022 purpose code 'COMC' when financing ordinary capital transfers, or 'EQUI' when handling equity-linked settlement. For non-EU wires, include the beneficiary's 22-digit ESEPA IBAN, the SL's legal name, the CIF/LEI in field 72, and a clear payment narrative such as 'SUBSCRIPCION DE PARTICIPACIONES - INVERSION EXTERIOR DIRECTA / DIRECT FOREIGN INVESTMENT'. If the amount exceeds EUR 1,000,000, the SL must file the 'Modelo DE/SI' statistical declaration to the Banco de España within one month after the transaction; the declaration is mandatory but not authorization-gated. Net capital proceeds may remain only in a demand-deposit account; they cannot be transferred to a fintech EMI without a documented business purpose. Incoming transfer verification requires simultaneous checking of sanction lists, the correct CIF tax validation, thenotarial deed certificate identifying subscriptions, and, where the investor is a company, its certified board resolution and registry certificate.For commercial-data supplier payments and licensing resettlement, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for non-EUR counterparties and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer or SEPA CT for EUR suppliers. All outbound payments must reference the underlying commercial invoice and, where necessary, attach an electronic certificate of invoice authenticity. For higher-value hardware, custom data-labor, or recurring hosting contracts, a revocable Commercial Letter of Credit (sight tenor) is available at Tier-1 banks, opened by MT700 and settled via URC/URR 522 and UCP600 with the presenting bank; this rail is recommended only for payments above EUR 250,000 or when trade terms require protected settlement. Cross-border disbursements to shell-company-like API resellers are subject to strict seller-KYC; payment orders lacking invoice evidence are blocked by Banco de España enforcement protocols. Settlement currencies accepted for disbursements are EUR, USD, GBP and CHF; any minor-currency payment not quoted by Banco de España will need a final invoice with FX conversion clause.EUR/USD outright forward contracts (vanilla, up to 24-month tenor) with a licensed Spanish credit institution or EU investment firm under MiFID II.EUR/GBP and EUR/CHF FX forwards for operating-currency exposures.Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market currencies (e.g., BRL, MXN, CLP, COP) if the counterparty is an EU-authorized bank and the transaction is cleared/confirmed by a reputable broker.Cross-currency swaps for long-term capital injection funding of infrastructure or large acquirer payments, permitted only with eligible BS/ECB-supervised banks and under anchor-party derivative collateral rules.FX options (call/put) used purely for reducing cash-flow downside volatility, subject to mandatory classification as per Bank of Spain Circular 5/2018 and EMIR clearing thresholds.

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Medium-to-High only as an ancillary rail; not a substitute for a licensed credit institution. Authorized EU/EEA Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) operating in Spain under the PSD2 and Royal Decree-Law 19/2018 may be used for low-balance operational accounts and cross-border collections, provided they hold a passportable license (e.g., to EBA register) and appoint a Spanish AML representative where required. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot offer capital escrow-taking deposit business, cannot extend credit, and client funds must be safeguarded in segregated pools; use of an unlicenced offshore EMI is prohibited and constitutes an AML/institutional red flag. The selected entity must support IBAN, SEPA, SWIFT MT103, and ideally Crypto-to-fiat on/off ramps with compliant CFATF/EBA travel-rule attestation.

Corporate income tax (CIT), box-by-box return breakdown, dividend WHT, and director personal liability.

Statutory corporate income tax (CIT)

25% for a Spanish-resident Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL). The general rate may not apply to qualifying new entities, microenterprises, small enterprises, or other specially regulated taxpayers.

Dividend withholding tax (WHT)

19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions and applicable double-tax treaty relief. Qualifying EU parent companies may obtain exemption under the Parent-Subsidiary regime, generally requiring a qualifying participation and satisfaction of holding-period, beneficial-owner, anti-abuse and other statutory conditions.

Mandatory Return Breakdown

Deadline: · Frequency:

Modelo 200: within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax period ends; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally 1–25 July. Modelo 202: generally 1–20 April, October and December. If the final day is not a business day, the applicable filing and payment rules may extend the deadline.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: Spanish related-party transactions are generally subject to the arm's-length principle. Simplified Local File documentation is generally required where aggregate related-party transactions exceed EUR 250,000 at market value with the same related person or entity during the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and documentation rules. A Master File is generally required for groups with net turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to applicable rules and exemptions. Additional documentation and information-return obligations may apply independently of these thresholds.

Economic substance scope: Spain does not operate a general standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Spanish substance, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, permanent-establishment, controlled-foreign-company and transfer-pricing rules remain relevant. An SL conducting public commercial web scraping and proxy/API gateway activities should substantiate personnel, decision-making, assets, data rights, contractual functions, cybersecurity controls, customer location and the allocation of value-creating functions. Lack of substance may undermine treaty benefits, deductions, residence positions or transaction pricing.

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax evasion, false returns or concealed income

Statutory sanction: Tax penalties are generally 50%–150% of the unpaid amount, depending on the infringement and aggravating factors, in addition to tax, interest and possible criminal prosecution. Tax fraud exceeding the statutory criminal threshold, generally EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period, may constitute a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine generally linked to the defrauded amount; aggravated cases can carry higher sanctions.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur civil or administrative liability where statutory conditions are met, including for culpable failure to ensure compliance or non-payment during dissolution. Criminal liability may attach to directors who participate in or direct the offence. Imprisonment is not automatic; travel restrictions require a competent authority's order and legal basis.
Transfer-pricing misstatement and non-documentation

Statutory sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income and assess additional tax and interest. Transfer-pricing documentation and reporting failures can attract statutory fixed or value-based penalties; the amount depends on the specific breach, adjustment and applicable penalty provisions.

Director personal liability: Directors may be liable for serious or repeated compliance failures where statutory requirements are met. Personal criminal exposure requires participation in conduct satisfying the applicable offence elements.
Artificial residence, shell arrangements or treaty abuse

Statutory sanction: Relief may be denied, withholding tax and corporate tax reassessed, and interest and applicable penalties imposed. Criminal consequences require conduct meeting the elements and thresholds of a criminal tax offence.

Director personal liability: Directors may face civil, administrative or criminal liability depending on their role and the statutory basis. Shareholder status alone does not establish personal liability.
Unlawful web scraping, data protection or intellectual-property infringement

Statutory sanction: Potential consequences include contractual damages, civil injunctions, intellectual-property remedies, data-protection administrative fines and, where criminal elements are met, criminal sanctions. GDPR administrative fines may reach EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher, for specified infringements.

Director personal liability: The SL is generally liable for corporate conduct, but directors may incur personal liability for their own unlawful acts, statutory duties or criminal participation. GDPR fines are imposed on the controller or processor, not automatically on individual directors.
AML, sanctions or cryptocurrency payment-control failure

Statutory sanction: Consequences depend on the applicable AML, sanctions and payment-services regime and may include administrative fines, asset freezes, authorization consequences and criminal penalties. A software/API business is not automatically an AML-obliged entity solely because it accepts cryptocurrency; its activities and regulatory status must be assessed.

Director personal liability: Directors may incur personal administrative or criminal liability for their own participation, consent, negligence where prescribed by law, or breach of specific supervisory duties. Personal travel restrictions and imprisonment require an applicable legal order or criminal judgment.
